What is the difference between the two readings?

hints: Look at the horizontal datum line on each sleeve: count whole $1\text{ mm}$ marks and then check if a $0.5\text{ mm}$ mark is also uncovered.
Recall micrometer reading = sleeve reading + thimble reading, where thimble divisions are $0.01\text{ mm}$ and are read where the datum line crosses the thimble scale.
Compare reading 1 near $1\text{ mm}$ with thimble near 13 against reading 2 near $12.5\text{ mm}$ with thimble near 47, then subtract the smaller from the larger.
walkthrough: Identify the rule: micrometer reading = main sleeve in $1\text{ mm}$ plus $0.5\text{ mm}$ if visible + thimble in $0.01\text{ mm}$.
Read reading 1: sleeve shows $1.0\text{ mm}$ with no extra $0.5\text{ mm}$ uncovered, thimble shows 13 divisions at the datum, so $1.0 + 0.13 = 1.13\text{ mm}$.
Read reading 2: sleeve shows $12.0\text{ mm}$ plus one $0.5\text{ mm}$ mark uncovered, thimble shows 47 divisions at the datum, so $12.0 + 0.5 + 0.47 = 12.97\text{ mm}$.
Find the difference: $12.97\text{ mm} - 1.13\text{ mm} = 11.84\text{ mm}$.

A.explanation: Too small by $1.50\text{ mm}$, from missing the $0.5\text{ mm}$ half-millimetre marks on one or both sleeves.

B.explanation: Equals $12.97\text{ mm} - 1.13\text{ mm} = 11.84\text{ mm}$ from correct sleeve plus thimble readings.

C.explanation: Too large by $0.50\text{ mm}$, from counting an extra half-millimetre on the sleeve of reading 1 or reading 2.

D.explanation: Too large by $1.00\text{ mm}$, from misreading the whole-millimetre sleeve scale by $1\text{ mm}$.
